title: Video interviews
examples: What is the best way to check my internet connection before a video interview?
Should I dress more formally for a video interview than I would in person?
How long should I plan for my answers during a virtual interview?

explain.say: First we will talk about setting up your space for the interview.
Next we will look at how to use the camera effectively during your talk.
Then we will discuss the importance of having helpful notes available to you.
For a real-life example imagine you are interviewing for a marketing role.
A common mistake is looking down at your notes too much while speaking.

faq.q: Should I use a physical notepad or digital notes?
faq.a: Using physical notes can feel more natural when you refer to them. You can also use digital notes if they are easily visible to you.
asks: Is it better to write notes by hand?
Can I use my laptop for notes?

faq.q: How far away should I sit from the camera?
faq.a: You should sit far enough away so that your head and shoulders fill the frame nicely. This keeps your body language visible to the interviewer.
asks: What is the ideal distance from the camera?
Should I be too close or too far?

faq.q: What is the best background to choose?
faq.a: Choose a background that is tidy and professional, like a plain wall or a bookshelf. Avoid anything distracting like clutter or people walking by.
asks: Can I use my living room as a background?

faq.q: How many notes should I prepare?
faq.a: Prepare only bullet points, not full sentences. This forces you to speak naturally and remember the core ideas.
asks: Should my notes be short or long?
What is the goal of my notes?

faq.q: What if I have poor lighting?
faq.a: Try to sit facing a window during the day for the best natural light. If that is not possible, use soft, indirect lamps.
asks: What if it is dark where I am?
How do I fix bad lighting?

facts: Ensure your background is clean and free from distractions.
Position yourself so the light source is in front of you, not behind you.
Notes should contain keywords and main ideas, not full scripts.
Maintain consistent eye contact with the camera lens, not the screen image.

quiz.say: When setting up for a video interview, where should the primary light source ideally be placed?
quiz.show: Light source in front of you.
quiz.why: Having light in front of you ensures your face is evenly lit and visible to the camera.

wrong.0: This creates uneven shadows across your face, which looks unprofessional.
wrong.1: Using only one side creates harsh, noticeable shadows on your face.
wrong.3: This will cause your face to appear shadowed or silhouetted.

quiz.say: What is the best way to use notes during the interview?

options.show: Use large print on the screen
options.say: Use large print on the screen

options.show: Keep notes hidden below the desk
options.say: Keep notes hidden below the desk

quiz.why: Keywords prompt your memory, allowing you to speak conversationally rather than reading.

wrong.0: Reading a script sounds unnatural and makes you seem unprepared.
wrong.1: This can make your notes look too formal and rigid.
wrong.2: If the interviewer cannot see your notes, you must look down to read them.

quiz.say: If you are worried about your background, what is the best first step?

options.show: Move to a different room entirely
options.say: Move to a different room entirely

options.show: Ask someone to clean it later
options.say: Ask someone to clean it later

quiz.why: A clean, simple background directs the interviewer's focus entirely onto you and your answers.

wrong.1: These filters can sometimes look artificial or glitchy on video.
wrong.2: This might disrupt your planned setup or lighting conditions.
wrong.3: You must prepare the space before the interview starts to ensure readiness.
